fundamental.headline: Business in a heavy investment phase, and expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 15% over the last year. Negative free cash flow because the company is investing heavily in growth (capex 27% of revenue, up from 17%); margins are improving, but sales growth has slowed, so the payoff isn't showing yet.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 75% of the last 5 years. However, it looks cheaper than similar companies once growth is considered.
drivers: It is spending heavily on new capacity (much of it AI), faster than sales are growing; the payoff isn't proven yet.
news: Recent earnings/results news is bad news for the company; the stock hasn't reacted much yet, and it could matter for months.
Recent deal/M&A news is news with no clear direction for the company; the stock hasn't reacted much yet, and it could matter for months.
fundamental.take: Profits are holding up, but cash is going into new capacity and the payoff isn't proven yet: the price already assumes it works, so there's little room for disappointment. This is research, not personal advice.

timing.label: No rush
timing.text: Nothing urgent in the next few weeks.

news_impact: How it could affect things: Touches sales growth, profit margins and valuation. Reported results test the growth and margin assumptions in the price.
What would confirm or break it: Confirm: the next report repeats the trend; Break: the next report reverses the trend.
Magnitude: insufficient history of similar events for this company.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 33% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (3%), because current free cash flow is negative). For comparison, sales grew 15% last year; 13%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 12% (3 years ago 12%, about the same) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $12 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 22% (3 years ago 11%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $28.2B, up 12% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Receivables (money customers still owe) up 61% vs quarterly sales up 12% (days to collect 31 → 44). Customers may be paying more slowly, or sales were pulled forward.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 13%/yr over 3 years and 12%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 13% vs a 5-year range of 2–13% (median 9%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: No buybacks or dividends reported over the last 12 months. Share count up 0.8% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $10.67, up 2% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 19 analysts raised, 10 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $12.80, up 1% in 90 days (down 1% in the last 30); 10 analysts raised, 18 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers
deeper.text: Compared with 5 peers (MSFT, GOOGL, ORCL, META, IBM): sales growth 15% vs a median of 22%; operating margin 13% vs 33%; price/sales 3.5× vs 6.5×.

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: North America 56% of sales, up 6%; AWS 23% of sales, up 39%; International 21% of sales, up 5%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $18.5M, 100% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

deeper.title: New risk factors
deeper.text: No new risk-factor headings in the latest annual report (21 headings, vs 21 the year before).

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: -3% vs a year ago · $12.33 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share fell 3% while sales grew 12%: costs are rising faster than sales.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Missed forecasts last quarter by 3%; another miss would suggest the business is weaker than expected.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 12% from a year ago but slowing (from 17% two quarters ago): the fastest growth may be behind it.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $13 of operating profit, up from $11 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Free cash flow is negative: it's spending more (often on new capacity) than the business brings in.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 21× last year's profit (lower than 95% of the last 5 years; in line with peers' 21); 24× next year's forecast, so profits are expected to fall.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: Management's outlook is roughly in line with what analysts expected.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects next, from its 8-K earnings release; compared with consensus where available.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is up 2% in 90 days (19 raised, 10 cut lately): forecasts are steady.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
